$comment: State income tax withholding on pension, annuity and IRA payments, by state of the payee's residence. Each state's rule comes from that state's revenue agency; every state not listed here, and every state marked not_modelled, produces no state line and a warning saying so. 4 U.S.C. 114 bars a state from taxing retirement income of a nonresident, so only the payee's own state ever withholds.

AL.notes: Alabama income tax is not required to be withheld from retirement distributions or pensions; voluntary withholding is permitted at the payee's request.

sources.title: Alabama Admin. Code r. 810-3-75-.04, Voluntary Withholding

AR.notes: Periodic payments are withheld as wages on the Arkansas tables; with no AR4P the payer withholds as married with three allowances. Nonperiodic payments 3%, eligible rollover distributions a mandatory 5%. The payee cannot name a dollar amount, only an additional amount.

sources.title: Arkansas Form AR4P (R 12/04/2025) and instructions

AZ.notes: Voluntary. The payee picks 0.5% to 3.5% of the taxable amount in half-point steps, plus an optional extra amount per payment (A.R.S. 43-404).

sources.title: Arizona Form A-4P (2026), Request for Voluntary Withholding on Retirement Income

CA.notes: Withheld unless the payee elects out. With no form the payer may use the California schedules as a married payee with three allowances, or 10% of the federal withholding; this uses the 10% method. The payee may instead name allowances, a dollar amount or elect none. Nothing is withheld for a payee who lives outside California.

sources.title: EDD DE 231P, Withholding from Pensions, Annuities, and Certain Other Deferred Income
EDD DE 4P (Rev. 46, 1-26)

CT.notes: A Connecticut-resident payee with no Form CT-W4P is withheld at 6.99% with no exemption. With a withholding code on CT-W4P, periodic payments use the Connecticut tables. Nonperiodic payments are 6.99% unless the payee enters code E ($0, or a fixed amount). A distribution of the entire account balance is 6.99% with no exemption.

sources.title: CT DRS, Pension Payers
Form CT-W4P (Rev. 12/21)

periodic.reason: The District's published guidance read for this build covers lump-sum distributions only.

otherwise.reason: The District's published rule read for this build withholds at 10.75% on lump-sum distributions of a whole account; other nonperiodic payments were not confirmed.
The District's published rule read for this build withholds at 10.75% on lump-sum distributions of a whole account; other payments were not confirmed.

DC.notes: The District requires withholding at its highest rate (10.75%) for DC residents on lump-sum distributions from retirement accounts, except amounts previously taxed and direct trustee-to-trustee transfers or rollovers.

sources.title: DC OTR, 2024 FR-900NP instructions

DE.reason: Delaware's pension office offers its own form; the Division of Revenue's payer rule was not confirmed.

GA.notes: Periodic pension and annuity payments are withheld as wages unless the recipient elects not to on Form G-4P (O.C.G.A. 48-7-101). Nonperiodic payments are withheld only when the payee elects it, in an amount no lower than wage withholding would be.

sources.title: Georgia DOR 2023 Employer's Tax Guide: pension and annuity payments
Georgia Form G-4P (Rev. 06/03/26)

IA.notes: Withheld at 3.8% unless the payee qualifies for the retirement-income exclusion (age 55 or older, disabled, or a surviving spouse of someone who would have), in which case the administrator is generally not required to withhold. Not required when no federal withholding is required.

sources.title: Iowa Department of Revenue, Withholding Tax Information (IAC 701-307.1(2))

ID.notes: Payers of retirement income are not required to withhold Idaho income tax.

sources.title: Idaho State Tax Commission, withholding: retirement-income payers

IL.notes: Withholding on pensions and annuities is by voluntary agreement only.

sources.title: Illinois Publication 131 / Form IL-941 instructions: voluntary withholding agreements

IN.notes: Voluntary: the payee requests withholding in writing on Form WH-4P.

sources.title: Indiana Information Bulletin #13 and Form WH-4P

KS.reason: Kansas follows federal withholding (required when federal is required, voluntary when federal is), but the guide does not state a method for pension payments.

LA.notes: Withholding on pensions, retirement income and annuities is not required (R.S. 47:111(A)(9)); a recipient may ask for it.

sources.title: Louisiana Department of Revenue FAQ: Does Louisiana require withholding on pensions, retirement income, and annuities?

nonperiodic.reason: The Massachusetts withholding rate for nonperiodic payments was not confirmed from a current document (Form M-4P is Rev. 1/08).

eligibleRollover.reason: The Massachusetts withholding rate for eligible rollover distributions was not confirmed from a current document (Form M-4P is Rev. 1/08).

MA.notes: Massachusetts withholding applies to pension payments unless the payee has elected out of federal withholding; with no Form M-4P it is based on zero exemptions. Payments to a nonresident from certain plans are not subject to tax (4 U.S.C. 114).

sources.title: Massachusetts Form M-4P

MD.notes: Maryland requires withholding only on eligible rollover distributions that carry mandatory federal withholding: 7.75% (Tax-General 10-908(f)). On any other annuity or retirement distribution it withholds only when the payee asks, for a fixed amount of at least $5 a month on Form MW507P.

sources.title: Maryland Administrative Release No. 41, Withholding on Designated Distributions from Retirement Plans
Maryland Form MW507P

ME.notes: If payments from an employer-sponsored retirement plan carry federal withholding, Maine tax must also be withheld unless the payee elects out of Maine withholding. Periodic payments use the Maine wage methods; lump sums and nonperiodic payments, IRA and 401(k) distributions a flat 5%. Pensions and annuities paid to a nonresident are not withheld.

sources.title: Maine Revenue Services, 2026 Withholding Tables for Individual Income Tax and Instructions, table of common items of income

MI.notes: Mandatory on taxable pension distributions except as the payee directs on an MI W-4P. With no MI W-4P: 4.25% of the taxable amount. With one, 4.25% after the personal-exemption allowance claimed. Recipients born before 1946 follow separate limits that are not modelled.

sources.title: Michigan 2026 Income Tax Withholding Guide (446)
Michigan: Withholding for Pension Administrators FAQ

MN.notes: Minnesota residents are withheld at 6.25% unless the payee gives Form W-4MNP, which can choose a percentage, an amount, allowances (periodic payments use the Minnesota tables) or zero. The payer must request a W-4MNP before starting the 6.25% default.

sources.title: Minnesota 2026 Withholding Tax Instructions and Tables

MO.notes: Voluntary for the recipient; the plan administrator must withhold if the recipient asks (Form MO W-4P).

sources.title: Missouri DOR withholding FAQ: pension withholding is voluntary

MS.notes: Retirement income, pensions and annuities are not subject to Mississippi income tax, so nothing is withheld.

sources.title: Mississippi DOR business tax FAQ

NC.notes: Required when federal withholding is required on a payment to a North Carolina resident. Periodic payments: as a single payee with no allowances unless Form NC-4P says otherwise. Nonperiodic and eligible rollover distributions: 4% of the distribution; the payee can opt out of the nonperiodic rate but not of the rollover rate.

sources.title: North Carolina 2026 Income Tax Withholding Tables and Instructions for Employers, Section 6

ND.notes: Voluntary: only if the recipient requests it and the payer agrees.

sources.title: North Dakota Income Tax Withholding & Information Returns Guideline

NE.notes: Follows the federal method. Periodic payments: as wages on the Nebraska tables with the payee's W-4N. Nonperiodic payments and eligible rollover distributions that carry federal withholding: 3.5% of the distribution. No Nebraska withholding when none is withheld federally.

sources.title: Nebraska 2026 Circular EN, Pensions and Annuities
Nebraska Reg-21-004.06

NJ.notes: Voluntary: withholding starts only when the payee files Form NJ-W-4P.

sources.title: New Jersey Form NJ-W-4P, Certificate of Voluntary Withholding
NJ-WT Income Tax Withholding Instructions

NM.notes: New Mexico does not require payers to withhold on pensions and annuities unless the payee asks.

sources.title: New Mexico FYI-104, New Mexico Withholding Tax

NY.notes: Payers are not required to withhold; the annuitant may request it on Form IT-2104-P (at least $5 a month, and not enough to cut the payment below $10).

sources.title: New York Form IT-2104-P, Annuitant's Request for Income Tax Withholding
Tax.NY.gov: information for retired persons

OK.notes: Periodic payments are withheld as wages; with no Form OK-W-4-P the payer withholds as married with three allowances. Nonperiodic payments, including eligible rollover distributions, are withheld at the top marginal income tax rate (4.5% for 2026, the top rate in the OW-2 tables). The payee can choose no withholding on either form.

sources.title: Okla. Admin. Code 710:90-1-13, Pensions, annuities, and certain other deferred income
Oklahoma OW-2 percentage method tables (top bracket 4.5%)

OR.reason: Oregon pension payers commonly default to 8% on lump sums, but Oregon's own payer rule was not found.

PA.reason: Pennsylvania's guidance read for this build does not address payer withholding on retirement distributions.

nonperiodic.reason: Virginia's published guidance read for this build covers periodic payments on Form VA-4P; the rate for nonperiodic distributions was not confirmed.

eligibleRollover.reason: Virginia's published guidance read for this build covers periodic payments on Form VA-4P; the rate for eligible rollover distributions was not confirmed.

VA.notes: Payers of pensions and annuities to Virginia residents withhold on the Virginia tables; with no Form VA-4P, as if no exemptions were claimed. Financial institutions are not payers for IRA or SEP distributions.

sources.title: Virginia Tax, Income Tax Withholding Guide for Employers (Rev. 10/26)
Form VA-4P instructions

VT.notes: Required when federal withholding is required or the payee elects it and does not claim exemption from Vermont. Periodic payments use the Vermont tables; nonperiodic payments are estimated at 30% of the federal withholding.

sources.title: Vermont Department of Taxes, Withholding Tax Instructions

WI.notes: Pension and retirement income are not wages under Wisconsin law, so withholding is not required; a recipient who asks in writing can have it withheld.

sources.title: Wisconsin Department of Revenue, Withholding Tax Guide (Publication W-166, January 2026)
Wisconsin Withholding Tax Update, October 2025
